correctness.rationale: From the distributional support constraint, Σ_j R_j μ=c dθ and μ≥0 imply μ absolutely continuous, 0≤ρ≤c, S_kρ=c. First Fourier moments vanish for curvature measures of closed curves and ensure solvability of h+h″=ρ modulo translations. If an orbit has two coordinates ≥δ on a measurable set, a nonzero bounded perturbation supported on three subsets solves both first-moment conditions and swaps curvature between two orbit entries without violating positivity; hence such a body is not extreme. A 0/c-valued curvature field is extreme pointwise. Fourier support-area identity is strictly concave on fixed mean and zero-first-moment fields, so every area minimizer is extreme; fixed-perimeter Blaschke selection establishes existence. The k3 lens orbit sum and exact segment area were independently checked, but not used to establish the universal theorem.
residual_risks: The existence argument relies on fixed-Steiner-center compactness, not minimizing on an unrestricted translation orbit.
